question: Can global loss-landscape diagnostics predict whether a dense model should be trained with more or less optimization noise before magnitude pruning, and thereby guide checkpoint and SAM-hyperparameter selection?

key_findings.claim: Pruned networks empirically separate into three regimes using linear mode connectivity and output CKA.
key_findings.evidence: Two copies of the same pruned mask are retrained under different SGD noise. A negative training-error barrier along their linear weight interpolation defines poorly connected Regime I. Near-zero barriers define Regime II, which output CKA divides into dissimilar II-A and similar II-B. The main PreResNet-20/CIFAR-10 heatmaps show an abrupt LMC boundary and a smoother CKA gradient across density and dense-training epoch.

key_findings.claim: The direction of the reported temperature effect changes with pruning density.
key_findings.evidence: For heavy pruning, fewer dense-training epochs, smaller batches, or larger SAM neighborhoods often reduce final error and move models from negative-LMC Regime I toward II-A. For light pruning, lower claimed temperature often improves output similarity and performance within Regime II-B. This pattern recurs in the displayed density/epoch and density/batch grids.

key_findings.claim: Epoch, batch-size, and SAM-radius sweeps are phenomenological control axes, not isolated measurements of a common physical temperature.
key_findings.evidence: Fewer epochs changes optimization progress and compute. Batch-size experiments hold the number of iterations fixed, so the 16-to-512 sweep changes examples processed by 32x as well as gradient noise. SAM radius changes the objective and doubles gradient work. No mapping places these controls on a calibrated common scale, so the statistical-mechanics terminology organizes observations but does not identify a thermodynamic variable or causal noise effect.

key_findings.claim: A fixed LMC threshold predicts when an initial dense-training choice should move toward higher temperature in the studied grids.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm 1 labels a pruned model Regime I when LMC is below -0.05 and recommends an increased temperature; otherwise it retains the conventional low-temperature choice. Across epoch/batch versus density/width/depth plots, the highlighted negative-LMC cases generally coincide with cases where the tested larger-temperature alternative lowers final error.

key_findings.claim: The threshold and direction rule are evaluated largely on the same experimental families from which they were chosen.
key_findings.evidence: The -0.05 threshold is selected empirically from the paper's architecture/dataset taxonomy, and the method is verified by comparing against other points in those same sweeps. No preregistered threshold, held-out task family, prospective one-shot decision, calibration curve, false-positive rate, or confidence interval is reported. The result is strong retrospective correlation evidence, not yet a validated universal predictor.

key_findings.claim: Short-retraining LMC/CKA can choose a dense checkpoint close to a full train-prune-retrain grid at lower sparse-retraining cost.
key_findings.evidence: Given 16 epoch checkpoints or 13 batch-size checkpoints, Algorithm 2 first uses dense test error, then—only if the chosen sparse model has poor LMC—re-trains every candidate for two epochs and selects by short-run sparse error. The training-only variant proposes CKA instead. Figures 4 and 16 show selections near the 160-epoch-per-candidate grid-search envelope and better than choosing solely by dense-model error in heavy-pruning regimes.

key_findings.claim: The advertised test-data-free selection algorithm is internally inconsistent in the paper's pseudocode.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.2 says Algorithm 2.1 only requires training data, yet Appendix Algorithm 2.1 explicitly takes dense-model test errors and initializes its candidate with argmin_i error_test(Theta_i) before using LMC/CKA. This may be a copy-and-paste specification error, but as written the procedure is not test-free. Algorithm 2 openly uses test error, which would also be invalid model selection unless 'test' is replaced by a validation split.

key_findings.claim: The method reduces full sparse retraining but still requires material diagnostic computation and pre-existing dense candidates.
key_findings.evidence: LMC/CKA require pruning, retraining two same-mask copies, evaluating the entire training set along many interpolation points for LMC, and 6,400 training samples for CKA. Model selection assumes all 13-16 dense checkpoints/models already exist and, in Regime I, briefly retrains every candidate. The claimed 'twice the efficiency' comparison to a two-point grid omits these costs and is not backed by measured FLOPs, GPU-hours, or wall time.

key_findings.claim: SAM's pruning effect is regime-dependent in the reported experiments.
key_findings.evidence: At 7% density, SAM with rho 0.6 improves error, LMC, and CKA when the SGD baseline lies in Regime I but provides negligible improvement in Regime II. Across densities, rho 0.8 helps 5-10% models and slightly harms 20-80% models; choosing the rho with highest CKA selects the best displayed test-error setting.

key_findings.claim: The three-regime pattern is visually replicated across several small-scale variations, but some extensions use only one dense seed.
key_findings.evidence: Appendices vary DenseNet-40, VGG-19, CIFAR-100, SVHN, global magnitude pruning, Adam/SGD combinations, and WMT14 Transformer-base translation. Main image experiments average three dense and three sparse seeds, while the Adam and translation extensions use one dense seed and three retraining seeds. Heatmaps and curves show similar qualitative boundaries, but uncertainty is not plotted.

key_findings.claim: The released code covers the central image-classification pipeline and metrics but has broken portability and incomplete study coverage.
key_findings.evidence: At commit b38c972, the repository contains PreResNet/DenseNet/VGG training, uniform/global magnitude pruning, SAM, retraining, LMC, CKA, sweep generation, pinned core dependencies, downloadable checkpoints/metrics, and a plotting notebook. There are no tests; the documented script name does not exist, the actual stage script hard-codes the author's absolute cluster path and only invokes training, and code for WMT14, Adam extensions, model-selection algorithms, and prospective threshold evaluation is absent.

method.core_idea: Diagnose the post-pruning optimization basin with two global metrics and use the resulting regime label to choose the direction of dense-training regularization or checkpoint selection.
method.mechanism: Dense models are trained over epoch, batch-size, width, optimizer, or SAM-radius sweeps, magnitude-pruned to target density, and retrained from the same mask under independent SGD noise. Linear interpolation of two sparse solutions yields an error-barrier LMC score; CKA compares their output matrices. Negative LMC identifies Regime I, near-zero LMC plus low/high CKA identifies II-A/II-B. Threshold rules recommend early stopping or smaller batches, select dense candidates after two sparse epochs, or choose SAM rho by CKA.
assumptions: Epoch count, batch size, and SAM radius are monotone proxies for a shared temperature-like quantity.
Pruned density, width, or depth is a meaningful load-like quantity.
Two SGD-noise retraining runs adequately characterize the relevant global landscape.
A linear path is representative of connectivity even when nonlinear low-loss paths may exist.
Training classification error is an appropriate barrier function for LMC.
Output-logit CKA is predictive of final sparse-model generalization.
The empirically selected LMC threshold -0.05 transfers across tasks and architectures.
Candidate dense models or checkpoints are already available when model selection begins.
Validation data can replace every use labeled test error in deployment.

techniques.role: Measures the worst training-error barrier on a linear path between two sparse solutions.
Measures functional similarity between independently retrained sparse copies.
Partitions load-control grids into connectivity/similarity regimes.
Maps negative LMC to a recommendation for higher claimed temperature.
Screens dense candidates with two sparse fine-tuning epochs instead of full retraining.
Selects SAM radius using output similarity after pruning.
Creates uniform or global unstructured magnitude masks at target density.
Visualizes final error and diagnostics across density and training-control sweeps.

evaluations.setting: PreResNet-20 on CIFAR-10 across 16 dense-training epochs and nine post-pruning densities
evaluations.metric: Final test error, normalized test error, LMC, and output CKA
evaluations.result: A sharp LMC boundary and smoother CKA boundary align with a three-region final-error pattern
evaluations.baseline: Uniform magnitude pruning with conventional train-to-completion checkpoints

evaluations.setting: Epoch/batch temperature crossed with density/width/depth load controls
evaluations.metric: Whether an LMC threshold predicts the sign of the final-error change
evaluations.result: Negative-LMC settings generally benefit from the tested higher-temperature alternative
evaluations.baseline: Always train to completion or retain the initial batch setting

evaluations.setting: Selecting among 16 epoch or 13 batch-size dense candidates for nine target densities
evaluations.metric: Final sparse test error and sparse retraining epochs
evaluations.result: LMC plus two-epoch error/CKA selection approaches full 160-epoch grid search, especially improving low-density cases
evaluations.baseline: Dense-model test-error selection and full train-prune-retrain grid search

evaluations.setting: SAM versus SGD and rho sweep across pruning regimes
evaluations.metric: Final test error, LMC, and CKA
evaluations.result: Large rho helps heavily pruned Regime-I models but slightly harms lightly pruned models; max-CKA chooses the best displayed rho
evaluations.baseline: SGD, rho zero, and fixed SAM radius

evaluations.setting: Architecture, dataset, pruning-rule, and optimizer extensions
evaluations.result: DenseNet-40, VGG-19, CIFAR-100, SVHN, global magnitude pruning, and Adam/SGD variants show analogous trends
evaluations.baseline: PreResNet-20, CIFAR-10, uniform magnitude pruning, and SGD

evaluations.setting: Transformer-base on 1.28M WMT14 German-English pairs across ten epochs and six densities
evaluations.result: Fewer dense-training epochs help low densities while more epochs help high densities
evaluations.baseline: One dense seed per epoch and three sparse retraining seeds

limitations: The model is phenomenological and supplies no derivation or predictive law connecting control values to regime boundaries.
Epoch, batch size, and SAM radius simultaneously change compute, data exposure, objective, and noise rather than isolating temperature.
The LMC threshold is chosen and assessed on substantially overlapping experimental families.
No prospective held-out-task evaluation reports sensitivity, specificity, regret, or threshold calibration.
The nominal training-only Algorithm 2.1 still consumes test errors in its published pseudocode.
Diagnostic cost includes two sparse retrains, full-training-set interpolation sweeps, and CKA inference, but measured wall time/FLOPs are absent.
Uncertainty bars and per-seed dispersion are absent from the heatmaps and selection plots.
Most evidence uses small vision models and unstructured magnitude pruning; structured, movement, dynamic, and one-shot LLM pruning are untested.
The translation and Adam extensions use only one dense-training seed.
Density is reported as parameter sparsity without realized memory, latency, energy, or hardware speedup.
The code omits several appendix studies and model-selection procedures, has no tests, and its orchestration script is not portable.
failure_modes: A negative straight-line barrier can coexist with a low-loss nonlinear path, misclassifying global connectivity.
Two retraining seeds can give an unstable LMC/CKA estimate near the threshold.
A threshold calibrated on CIFAR convolutional models can fail on normalization-heavy Transformers or transfer learning.
Holding iterations fixed while changing batch size can make apparent temperature effects reflect extra examples and compute.
Selecting on test error overstates final performance and invalidates generalization estimates.
High output CKA can preserve the same systematic errors and need not imply a better sparse model.
Uniform/global magnitude masks may not turn nominal sparsity into deployment acceleration.
Computing diagnostic curves can cost more than trying a cheap alternative checkpoint when models are small.
SAM radius can affect training stability or learning-rate compatibility independently of the proposed regime.
reusable_insights: Treat prunability as a property of the dense checkpoint and target sparsity jointly, not as a fixed model score.
Use short sparse-retraining probes to screen checkpoints before committing to full recovery training.
Validate any pruning diagnostic prospectively on held-out architecture-task-pruner families.
Deconfound optimization noise from update count, examples processed, and wall-clock compute in batch/epoch studies.
Replace test error in selection pseudocode with a declared validation split and reserve test data for one final evaluation.
Report diagnostic overhead and realized hardware savings alongside parameter density.
Combine connectivity and functional-similarity measures because either alone collapses distinct behaviors.
Publish threshold calibration curves and abstain when diagnostic uncertainty overlaps a regime boundary.
open_questions: Does -0.05 remain predictive on held-out modern architectures, datasets, and structured or activation-aware pruners?
Can temperature proxies be replaced by a measurable common noise scale under compute-matched training?
Can LMC/CKA be estimated from one sparse trajectory or a few minibatches without two retraining copies?
What causal mechanism links output similarity after pruning to final generalization?
Can uncertainty-aware regime classification outperform a fixed threshold?
Do analogous regimes predict quantization, distillation, low-rank compression, and LLM sparsification?
Does regime-informed pruning improve measured latency and energy on sparse hardware?
Can the training-only model-selection algorithm be specified and tested without any hidden test-set use?

competitive_landscape.title: When to Prune? A Policy towards Early Structural Pruning
competitive_landscape.relationship: A direct competing policy for deciding when dense training has progressed enough to prune without an oracle grid.
competitive_landscape.difference: It monitors stability of neuron-importance rankings, uses structured pruning, and reports ImageNet GPU-cost savings; the reviewed paper diagnoses post-pruning basin connectivity and can recommend either earlier or later training depending on target density.

competitive_landscape.title: Train Flat, Then Compress: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Learns More Compressible Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: The closest prior claim that SAM/flat-minimum training systematically improves compressibility.
competitive_landscape.difference: It evaluates BERT pruning, quantization, and distillation and treats SAM as broadly beneficial; the reviewed work argues SAM is beneficial only in some post-pruning regimes and tunes rho with CKA.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Predictability of Pruning Across Scales
competitive_landscape.relationship: An earlier predictive model of magnitude-pruned error over width, depth, dataset size, and density.
competitive_landscape.difference: It fits an explicit scaling-law functional form across large ImageNet models; the reviewed paper predicts the direction of dense-training hyperparameter adjustment from measured post-pruning geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
competitive_landscape.relationship: The direct methodological precursor connecting SGD-noise stability, linear mode connectivity, and successful sparse subnetworks.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies when winning tickets become stable, including ImageNet ResNet-50/Inception-v3; the reviewed work combines LMC with output CKA to form three regimes and operational tuning rules.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A three-regime load-temperature taxonomy explains why higher-temperature dense training can either help or hurt pruning and yields practical LMC/CKA rules for tuning, model selection, and SAM.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper maps thousands of train-prune-retrain configurations, replicates qualitative boundaries across architectures/datasets/optimizers, and compares short-diagnostic selection with dense-error and full-grid baselines.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Combining post-pruning LMC and functional CKA into an operational, density-dependent checkpoint rule is a useful and distinctive synthesis. Its status is best described as an empirical diagnostic heuristic: the physical analogy is not causal, selection-cost and test-use claims need correction, and prospective transfer beyond the calibration grids is the central missing validation.

reviewer_notes: Read and section-mapped all 20 cached pages, including every main/appendix heatmap, curve, algorithm, metric definition, implementation detail, robustness study, and reference. A rendered 5-by-4 full-document contact sheet showed 20 intact, correctly oriented pages and legible visual panels; the index reports 20/20 text pages and full_text_ok. I inspected the official repository at commit b38c9721db5cabb8c664666811c1f7c5f8e83cf2: central CIFAR train/prune/retrain, LMC/CKA, SAM, sweep, checkpoint-download, and visualization components exist and core dependencies are versioned. There are no automated tests; the README calls a nonexistent three_regime.sh, the available three_stage.sh hard-codes the author's cluster path and stops after dense training, and several paper studies/algorithms are absent. The paper's training-only Algorithm 2.1 was checked directly against its pseudocode and still uses test error. Current competitor versions were checked on official arXiv records on 2026-08-23. No shared generated artifacts were rebuilt.
